title: Beeswax jar candle with lavender
subtitle: A naturally scented beeswax container candle
excerpt: A container candle of pure beeswax with lavender essential oil. Beeswax burns cleaner and longer than soy or paraffin but holds less fragrance. Requires a larger wick than soy for the same jar size. Makes one 200 ml jar.
sourceNotes: Beeswax candle properties and wick sizing: general candlemaking reference, National Candle Association (candles.org) technical guidance. Lavender EO in beeswax candles: standard aromatherapy reference. Beeswax pour temperature: approximately 70°C for container beeswax. Lavender essential oil first-trimester and pet-safety notes: EMA HMPC monograph (2012).

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 jar candle (~200 ml jar, ~50 burn hours)
recipe.batchNotes: Three or four jars per session; beeswax sets faster than soy so work quickly at the pour stage.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cure one week before the first burn. The honey note in beeswax deepens slightly over the cure period.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Beeswax candles are effectively indefinite in shelf life: the wax itself does not go off. The lavender essential oil fades after 18 months; the natural honey note of the beeswax remains. Keep in a cool, dark place to prevent the wax yellowing.

glossaryTerms.definition: Beeswax melts at around 62 to 65°C, higher than soy wax (50°C) or paraffin (47 to 64°C depending on grade). This means beeswax burns hotter and longer per gram. It also requires a larger wick than soy wax for the same jar diameter, to sustain a full melt pool.

content.text: A container candle of pure beeswax scented with lavender essential oil. Beeswax has a natural honey note from the comb; it burns cleanly and for a long time. The

is higher than soy, so the pour temperature is higher (around 70°C) and the wax sets more quickly. Beeswax also holds less fragrance than soy; keep the essential-oil loading to 3 to 4% rather than the 6 to 8% that soy can accept.
Lavender essential oil is toxic to cats. Never leave a burning candle unattended.

items.prepNote: cotton wick; size up one size from what you would use in soy for the same jar (beeswax burns hotter)

content.text: Warm the jar to 60°C in a low oven. Fix the wick in the centre of the base. Lay across the centring bar.

Melt the beeswax in the pouring pitcher over a bain-marie until fully liquid. Cool to 68°C. Add the lavender essential oil and stir for 30 seconds. Pour immediately into the warm jar. Beeswax sets faster than soy; do not delay.

Beeswax shrinks as it cools and may leave a dip around the wick. Melt a small amount of extra wax and pour a second topping layer once the first has fully set. Trim the wick to 5 mm. Cure for one week.
Allow the melt pool to reach the jar edge on the first burn. Beeswax burns hotter than soy; trim the wick to 5 mm before each burn to prevent smoking.
Beeswax candles last indefinitely. The lavender essential oil fades after 18 months. Keep in a cool, dark place to prevent yellowing.
